title: K5 common-order correlated spectral covariance universality audit
frozen_hypothesis: Within the linearized K5 Gaussian surrogate, replacing independent/vertex-factorized edge widths by a single joint covariance with all six cycle-space eigenmodes scaling at the same spectral order eta^2 yields an invariant density exponent 6, independent of the positive-definite shape matrices on support and cycle space.
interpretation_if_pass: A common spectral order is sufficient to restore exponent uniqueness inside this explicitly correlated surrogate class; Iter419 path dependence came from unequal scaling orders, not merely covariance-shape anisotropy.
interpretation_if_fail: Even a common-order joint spectral covariance does not stabilize the surrogate exponent, so the regulator ambiguity is deeper than unequal edge/vertex scaling orders.
scope_guard: Not a derivation of the physical Toller/EPRL i-epsilon prescription, not a full causal vertex convergence theorem, and not D7 authorization.
